info.title: Identity Backend V2
info.description:
**Prove the device and register the username on People Chain.** API-compatible with the shipping iOS/Android clients.

### Validation flow

The iOS smoke drives this sequence end-to-end; each step gates the next:

1. `POST /api/v1/auth/challenges` — mint a single-use challenge
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/app-attest/attestations` — iOS App Attest (`202`, no-op in M0)
3. `POST /api/v1/auth/token` — sr25519 proof exchanged for a JWT
4. `POST /api/v1/usernames/available` — JWT-gated People Chain read
5. `POST /api/v1/usernames` — `202` outbox reservation

> **Attestation is disabled for M0.** Apple/Google verification is intentionally a no-op; the sr25519 account proof and People Chain reads still run end-to-end.

All non-2xx responses share the `ErrorResponse` envelope: `{ error, message }`.

get.summary: Publish the Ed25519 public key so siblings can verify tokens.
`GET /api/v1/attester` — the attester authority public key (`0x`+hex, public).

200.description: The on-chain attester account the backend writes as.

202.description: Accepted. No-op in M0 — payload is not verified against Apple/Google.

201.description: A fresh single-use challenge. No body required.

post.summary: Verify challenge + client proof and issue an access + refresh token pair.

200.description: Verified. Access JWT + opaque refresh token.

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token, returning a fresh access + refresh pair.

200.description: Rotated. New access JWT + new opaque refresh token.

401.description: Unknown, expired, or already-spent refresh token.

post.summary: Claim an invitation ticket for a DIM, returning a signature (JWT-gated).

200.description: Ticket claimed: the oldest `available` ticket of the `(dim, network)` pool, atomically flipped to `claimed`, with an sr25519 signature by the ticket key over the claimant's decoded 32-byte account id.

400.description: Body validation failed (RFC 9457 problem details with per-field `errors`); or plain-text `Malformed JSON in request body` when the body is not JSON.

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification (RFC 9457 problem details).

409.description: Ticket race lost — a concurrent request claimed the contended ticket.

422.description: Pool exhausted — no `available` ticket in the `(dim, network)` pool.

429.description: Per-subject rate limit exceeded (RFC 9457 problem details, with `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Request a DIM ticket for an address (JWT-gated).

200.description: Ticket accepted as `PENDING`; the single-instance chain writer registers it on People Chain asynchronously (poll the status route).

400.description: Body validation failed (RFC 9457 problem details with per-field `errors`); or plain-text `Malformed JSON in request body` when the body is not JSON. Note SS58 validity is NOT checked here — a well-formed but invalid address is a 500 (legacy quirk).

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification (RFC 9457 problem details).

409.description: The address already holds a ticket.

422.description: The inviter's on-chain invite quota is exhausted.

429.description: Per-subject rate limit exceeded (RFC 9457 problem details, with `Retry-After`).

500.description: Unexpected internal failure (opaque legacy body) — including an SS58-invalid `who`, which legacy validated in the shell, not the schema.

get.summary: Look up a DIM ticket's registration status (JWT-gated).

parameters.name: who
parameters.description: SS58 address the ticket was requested for (not validated — an arbitrary string is looked up verbatim, exactly like legacy).

200.description: The ticket's current status. DB `SUBMITTING` reports as `SUBMITTED` on the wire; `registered` is the deprecated boolean mirror of `status == "REGISTERED"`; `onchainData` is `null` until registration.

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification (RFC 9457 problem details).

404.description: No ticket row for this address.

429.description: Per-subject rate limit exceeded (RFC 9457 problem details, with `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Issue short-lived TURN credentials for WebRTC ICE negotiation (JWT-gated).

201.description: Credentials minted: `username` is `{unixExpiry}:{hexId}` (expiry = now + TTL), `password` is the base64 HMAC over `username` under the secret shared with the TURN relay (the coturn REST-API construction), `servers` echoes the configured ICE server list.

400.description: Body validation failed (RFC 9457 problem details with per-field `errors`); or plain-text `Malformed JSON in request body` when the body is present but not JSON. A request with no JSON content-type skips validation entirely and succeeds (legacy quirk).

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification (RFC 9457 problem details).

429.description: Per-subject rate limit exceeded (RFC 9457 problem details, with `Retry-After`).

post.description:
Order mirrors the sibling services: verified JWT (`401` problem details) →
body parse (`400` plain text on malformed JSON) → body validation (`400`
problem details with per-field `errors`) → per-subject rate limit (`429`
with `Retry-After`). Beyond that the relay always answers `200`: on provider
failure it preserves the legacy `success: false` body instead of an error
status.

200.description: Relay accepted the request. The push result is echoed verbatim from the provider — including the legacy behavior of returning `200` with `success: false` on provider failure, so a non-200 status never signals a delivery failure.

400.description: Body validation failed (RFC 9457 problem details with per-field `errors`); or plain-text `Malformed JSON in request body` when the body is not JSON.

401.description: Missing/malformed `Authorization` header or failed token verification (RFC 9457 problem details).

429.description: Per-subject rate limit exceeded (RFC 9457 problem details, with `Retry-After`).

AppAttestRequest.description:
iOS Apple App Attest key-registration payload. Shape-preserving; not verified
while `AUTH_ENABLED` is false.

keyId.description: Client key identifier from App Attest enrollment.

attestation.description: Base64 attestation object from the platform.

AttesterResponse.description: `{ attester }` — the on-chain attester authority public key.

attester.description: `0x`-hex sr25519 public key the backend writes registrations as.

AvailableRequest.description:
`{ usernames: [base, ...] }` — bases to validate and check on chain
(documentation mirror; the handler validates raw JSON).

usernames.description: Candidate base usernames to validate and check (max 100).

value.description: Per-base availability, keyed by the requested base username.

ChallengeResponse.description: `201` body: a fresh single-use challenge for the sr25519 proof flow.

challenge.description: Opaque base64 32-byte challenge; echoed back in the `Auth-Challenge` header.

Dotns.description: Optional DotNS reservation, parking a base label for later full-person use.

signedAt.description: Unix timestamp the reservation was signed at.

ErrorResponse.description:
The shared error envelope returned by every non-2xx response.

`error` is a stable machine code (see [`AppError`]); `message` is a
human-readable detail that may change. This type exists so the OpenAPI
document can reference a single error schema across all endpoints.

message.description: Human-readable detail; safe to log, not intended for programmatic use.

NameAvailability.description: Availability of a single base username.

RefreshRequest.description: `{ refreshToken }` — present a prior opaque refresh token to rotate it.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token issued by `/auth/token` or a prior refresh.

RegisterRequest.description:
The flat registration request (documentation mirror — the handler
validates raw JSON to reproduce the legacy zod error bodies).

candidateAccountId.description: SS58 beneficiary account that will own the username.

preferredDigits.description: Optional two-digit suffix, e.g. `"07"`; random-free if omitted.

candidateSignature.description: `0x`-hex 64-byte sr25519 signature proving control of the candidate.

RegisterResponse.description: `202` body: the reserved full username and its parts.

device_check_available.description:
Present only when the DeviceCheck free-slot gate applies (the
attestation slice; deferred).

Status.description: A liveness/health status body: `{ status, service }`.

TokenResponse.description: `{ token, refreshToken }` — the shape both auth token routes return.

usernames.description: Assigned usernames in deterministic continuation order.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when exhausted.

SearchUsername.description: One assigned username in the shipping mobile response shape.

accountId.description: People Chain account encoded as SS58.

username.description:
Full username when present, otherwise `base.digits` with the digits
rendered as an integer (`alice.1` for stored digits `01`) — the
frozen legacy quirk (`NumberFromString` decode before rendering).

status.description: Assignment state, always `ASSIGNED` for this projection.

onchainData.description: On-chain event position, always null because the snapshot has none.

createdAt.description: Time the projection first observed the account.

updatedAt.description: Time the projection last refreshed the account.

who.description: SS58 address to claim a ticket for (any valid SS58 prefix).

dim.description: DIM to claim a ticket for: `Game` or `ProofOfInk`.

ClaimResponse.description:
The frozen 200 claim body: the ticket keypair's public half plus the
sr25519 signature over the claimant's decoded account id.

publicKey.description: `0x`-hex 32-byte sr25519 public key of the claimed ticket.

inviter.description: SS58 address of the inviter that registered the ticket on-chain.

network.description: Network the ticket is registered on: `westend2`, `paseo`, or `polkadot`.

claimedBy.description: SS58 address the ticket was claimed for (echoes `who`).

createdAt.description: Ticket generation time (JS-style ISO, millisecond precision).

signature.description:
`0x`-hex 64-byte sr25519 signature by the ticket key over the raw
32-byte account id decoded from `who`.

remaining.description: Tickets still `available` in this `(dim, network)` pool after the claim.

CreateTicketRequest.description: `{ who, dim }` — the ticket request command.

who.description:
SS58 address to request a ticket for. Only non-emptiness is validated
here; SS58 validity is checked later (an invalid address is a 500 —
legacy quirk).

dim.description: DIM to request a ticket for: `Game` or `ProofOfInk`.

CreateTicketResponse.description:
The frozen 200 body of `POST /api/v1/dim-ticket`: the accepted `PENDING`
ticket (no `onchainData` key; the address echoes as both `ticket` and
`who`).

ticket.description: SS58 address of the ticket (echoes the requested `who`).

who.description: SS58 address who requested the ticket (same value as `ticket`).

inviter.description: SS58 address of the inviter whose on-chain quota funds the ticket.

network.description:
Network the ticket will be registered on: `westend2`, `paseo`, or
`polkadot`.

createdAt.description: Ticket creation time (JS-style ISO, millisecond precision).

OnchainData.description: On-chain registration data, present once a ticket is `REGISTERED`.

blockNumber.description: Block number of the registration event.

blockHash.description: Hash of the block containing the registration event.

eventIndex.description: Index of the registration event inside the block.

network.description:
Network the ticket is registered on: `westend2`, `paseo`, or
`polkadot`.

createdAt.description: Ticket creation time (JS-style ISO, millisecond precision).

updatedAt.description:
Last state-change time (JS-style ISO; a `PENDING` ticket reports the
response time — legacy quirk).

IssueRequest.description: `{ regionHint? }` — the issue command (the hint is reserved and ignored).

regionHint.description: Optional region hint (reserved for future use; accepted and ignored).

IssueResponse.description:
The frozen 201 body: coturn REST-API ephemeral credentials plus the ICE
server list.

servers.description: Configured ICE server URLs (`stun:` / `turn:` forms), echoed verbatim.

username.description:
`{unixExpiry}:{hexId}` — expiry is mint time + TTL; the id is 8 random
bytes hex-encoded.

password.description:
Base64 HMAC over `username` under the relay-shared secret (algorithm
per deployment config, default HMAC-SHA1).

NotifyErrorDoc.description: One per-device push error inside the `200` response.

device.description: Device token the error is about.

environment.description: APNs environment, when the provider distinguishes dev/prod.

status.description: Provider status (string or number), when present.

deviceToken.description: Recipient device token (APNs hex or FCM token); platform is auto-detected.

pushId.description: Opaque push id echoed to the client app (32 or 64 hex chars).

platform.description: Explicit platform override; auto-detected from the token when omitted.

bundlerId.description: APNs topic override (the app bundle id); VoIP derives `<topic>.voip`.

voip.description: Enable the iOS VoIP push type for a call.

NotifyResponseDoc.description: The frozen `200` push-result body (echoed from the provider).

success.description: Whether the provider accepted the push.

platform.description: Platform the notification was routed to.

sent.description: Number of notifications sent, when the provider reports it (APNs/FCM).

failed.description: Number of failed notifications, when the provider reports it (APNs).

errors.description: Per-device errors, on partial or full provider failure.

tags.name: Usernames
tags.description: Public username search over the finalized chain projection. Unauthenticated; IP rate-limited.

tags.name: Invitation Tickets
tags.description: Synchronous invitation-credential claims from a pre-staged, on-chain-registered sr25519 keypair pool. The route the shipping iOS/Android apps call for Game / ProofOfInk credentials.

tags.name: DIM Tickets
tags.description: Asynchronous DIM (Game / ProofOfInk) invitation-credential requests: a ticket is accepted as PENDING and registered on People Chain by the single-instance chain writer; clients poll the status route.

tags.name: TURN
tags.description: Short-lived TURN credentials for WebRTC ICE negotiation: the coturn REST-API construction (username = expiry:id, password = HMAC over the username) minted against a secret shared with the TURN relay. Stateless — nothing is stored.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Send a push notification to an iOS (APNs) or Android (FCM) device. Stateless verify-only relay: it authenticates the JWT and forwards the frozen mobile payload, returning the provider's result — including the legacy `200 success:false` on provider failure.
